checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One playable video lasts 8 seconds, within one frame of tolerance.
must.why: The clip is 8 s, and the sampled frames run up to 7.6 s.

must.item: All footage comes from jet-30s.mp4, without generated replacement scenes or speed changes.
must.why: The clip was regenerated by AI (LTX 2.5). It looks like jet footage but is re-rendered, not the original pixels. The one input frame shown, a ship on a cockpit screen, does not match the output frames, so I cannot confirm they come from the source.

must.item: The edit favors visible action or meaningful cockpit interaction over inactive lead-ins, pauses, or repetitive footage.
must.why: The frames show a two-jet formation flyby and a pilot with dialogue. This is visible action, but it was picked blindly.

must.item: Any cuts preserve understandable action and do not leave an included spoken line conspicuously chopped mid-word.
must.why: The subtitles look complete ("Rook, you with me?", "Right here, Vega."). I cannot hear the audio to check for mid-word chops.

must.item: Original audio accompanies the retained footage in sync, with no added narration, music, or text.
must.why: The clip has sound, but I cannot hear it. The subtitles seem to be burned in from the source.

faults.what: The output is a 480p AI re-render. It is softer than the original, and the pilot's helmet and face drift slightly between frames.
The window was chosen blind (the middle of the video), so it is not selected for action. It contains cuts between a formation shot and cockpit shots, with a subtitle that may be chopped.

summary: The output is an 8-second jet clip with a formation flyby and a pilot with subtitles, but it is a blind middle window re-rendered by AI at 480p, not a true trim or highlight cut.
